title: Removing a pro-prime-to-ell factor from condensed derived invariants
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology, and a finite intermediate field $E$. For $F=E,\Omega$, put $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$, using all continuous maps on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. For a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space $V$, put $V_F(S)=C(S,F\otimes_E V)$ with the finite-dimensional product norm topology. For a topological group $J$, write $\mathcal A_F(J)$ for internal $C_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] with an action of the condensed group $S\mapsto C(S,J)$; invariants are the equalizer imposing that action to be trivial, and $R\Gamma_J$ is their ordinary total right derived functor in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $B,L$ be profinite groups, and suppose every finite continuous quotient of $B$ has order prime to $\ell$. Let $V$ have a continuous $E$-linear $B\times L$-action whose $B$-image $Q$ is finite of order prime to $\ell$. Give $V^B$ its subspace topology and its residual $L$-action. The canonical inflation morphism
$$a_F:R\Gamma_L((V^B)_F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_{B\times L}(V_F),$$
induced by $B\times L\to L$ and $(V^B)_F\hookrightarrow V_F$, is an isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{C_F})$. On degree-zero invariants it is the inclusion, hence the identity after identifying both invariant objects. It is natural in continuous equivariant $E$-linear maps of $V$. For $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the square formed by $a_E$, $\operatorname{Res}a_\Omega$ and the canonical derived coefficient maps induced by $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ commutes. Here and below the coefficient map to a restricted derived invariant object is obtained by deriving the natural equality of invariants with scalar restriction. If $B$ is trivial, $a_F$ is the identity under the evident identifications.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-image-open-kernel-inflation] to obtain the open normal kernel $K$, the finite quotient $Q=B/K$, and the isomorphism $t_F:R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(V_F)\to R\Gamma_{B\times L}(V_F)$ for both $F$. By hypothesis $|Q|$ is prime to $\ell$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned steps 1–3, now isolated as open-kernel inflation

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-averaging-condensed-invariant-summand], $\Gamma_Q^L$ is exact and $(V^B)_F\cong V_F^Q$ through invariant inclusion. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] with $G=K=Q$, quotient $1$. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] makes its resolution map $V_F^Q[0]\to R\Gamma_Q^L(V_F[0])$ invertible. Its normalized equation $c_F b_F=R\Gamma_L(\eta_F)$ gives an isomorphism $b_F:R\Gamma_L((V^B)_F)\to R\Gamma_{Q\times L}(V_F)$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), returned steps 4–5: finite averaging input and exact-derived assembly

proof.text: The composite $t_F b_F$ has source $R\Gamma_L((V^B)_F)$ and target $R\Gamma_{B\times L}(V_F)$. The composition clause of [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] identifies it with the canonical inflation $a_F$ for $B\times L\to Q\times L\to L$ and the invariant inclusion. Thus $a_F$ is an isomorphism. Its degree-zero map is the original inclusion: the ordinary normalized transposes restrict codomain to invariants and their inverses compose with inclusion. Both source and target invariant submodules are the same $L$-fixed part of $V_F^B$, so this map is the identity after that identification.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 6

proof.text: All maps used are canonical resolution maps, normalized inflation maps, or invariant inclusions. For an equivariant continuous $E$-linear map $f:V\to W$, $f\rho_V(b)=\rho_W(b)f$ implies $f(V^B)\subseteq W^B$ and equality of the two composites with invariant inclusions. The naturality clause of [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison], applied directly to $a_F$ viewed as the single quotient $B\to1$, gives the requested naturality without choosing a common finite image or compatible bases. The coefficient clause of that node applied to $C_E\to C_\Omega$ and $v\mapsto1\otimes v$ gives $u_{B\times L}a_E=(\operatorname{Res}a_\Omega)u_L$. The invariant identifications of step 2 respect this map since $e_\Omega(1\otimes v)=1\otimes e_E(v)$, term by term in the same finite sum. Thus this is precisely the coefficient square in the statement, in ordinary condensed modules.

source.place: Paragraph (3), analytic tame-inertia input; agent expansion, step 7

proof.text: If $B=1$, then $K=Q=1$, both kernel augmentations and the normalized comparisons in [lem-sfb-derived-invariants-normal-subgroup-comparison] are identities; invariant inclusion is also the identity. The composite in step 3 is therefore the identity. If $V=0$ the constructions are zero, and if $V^B=0$ step 2 gives zero derived invariants for $Q\times L$ and hence step 1 gives zero derived invariants for $B\times L$. No completeness assertion about $\Omega$ has been used.
